rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Maximum rent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent only once by a limited amount each year: no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is less. The city states the maximum allowable increase is 2.87 percent for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Just cause evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, breaking the lease, or the landlord moving into the property. For certain eviction reasons, the landlord might have to help pay the tenant's moving costs.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
